correctness.rationale: The distinct k-line cover sentence has rank k+1 and separates q=k from all q>k for k=2,3. To close the equal-small-order case left implicit in the proof, choose two parallel classes as grid axes. Every other line is the graph of a permutation; there are q(q−1) such lines, which is exactly q! for q=2 and q=3, so the sorted incidence structure is fixed up to isomorphism. For q≥4, distinct point pairs have both a collinear and a noncollinear third point; for intersecting lines, a new direction provides both a line through their meeting and one missing it, while an already selected direction provides a distinct parallel; parallel pairs admit a third line of the same or a different direction. For a point and line, the only forced restriction for a new parallel through the point is when the point already lies on the line. The mixed point/line incidence masks on distinct pairs follow from the unique join or meet and the remaining pencil/line sizes. On the last move, a mask with at least two positive incidences has at most one candidate, and the stored incidences, collinearity, parallelism or concurrency determine its eligibility including equality with pinned elements. With exactly one positive incidence, at most two candidates are forbidden by the remaining pins; with none, for l opposite-sort pins the available pool before same-sort exclusions is at least q(q−l) for points or (q+1)(q−l) for lines, each greater than 3−l. Repetitions can be matched directly. This gives the four-round strategy without coordinates. Point plus line counts increase with q, and the F4 plane realizes 36.
